voice-support-agent.industryPersona: Travel, retail, SaaS, and service support leaders managing repetitive inbound calls while protecting access to human help.
jobs: Resolve a routine request without navigating an IVR tree
Recover gracefully from interruption, noise, or tool failure
Transfer the full context when confidence or policy requires a person
voice-support-agent.opportunity: Voice automation is valuable where call volume is high and the task is bounded. The commercial wedge is not “replace the contact center”; it is reducing repetitive handling time while measuring containment quality and safe escalation.
voice-support-agent.vision: A realtime support layer that sounds natural, acts only through approved tools, and treats escalation as a successful outcome when automation is uncertain.
hypotheses: Interruptible dialogue will reduce caller frustration versus turn-locked IVR flows
Two high-volume intents can create measurable value before broad intent coverage
Handoff quality matters more than maximum containment
features: Realtime turn detection and interruption recovery
Reasoned handoff with transcript and completed steps
voice-support-agent.modelStrategy: Use streaming speech recognition, a low-latency conversational model, and server-side tool policies. The model proposes actions; a deterministic gateway validates identity, arguments, permissions, and confirmation requirements.
nonFunctional: Target sub-second first audio where the stack permits
Graceful degradation on packet loss and silence
Consent, recording, and retention controls by market
Trace every tool request and handoff reason
voice-support-agent.buildBuy: Buy telephony/media transport and commodity speech primitives; build the business policy, tool contracts, escalation logic, evaluation set, and operational analytics that differentiate the product.
voice-support-agent.commercial: Start with a paid discovery and call-flow audit, then a bounded pilot for one queue. Price implementation around integrations, coverage hours, evaluation depth, and support—not a guaranteed cost-saving percentage.
roadmap: One read-only account tool plus appointment booking
Agent desktop handoff and supervisor QA
voice-support-agent.evidence: The lab below is deterministic and browser-only. It demonstrates the intended state machine; it does not place a call or invoke a speech model.

support-chatbot.industryPersona: SaaS support and CX product teams whose assistants answer policy questions, inspect accounts, and hand work to agents.
jobs: Get a grounded answer without repeating context
Complete a safe account lookup or recover when it fails
Reach a human with a concise, accurate case summary
support-chatbot.opportunity: Support teams need more than FAQ deflection. A credible product combines grounded answers, stateful workflows, tool validation, and escalation analytics.
support-chatbot.vision: A stateful assistant that earns trust by showing its limits, validating every external action, and preserving the customer journey across automation and people.
hypotheses: A graph-based workflow reduces failure ambiguity compared with one large prompt
Explicit attempt counters improve recovery from repeated tool failures
Evidence-linked responses improve both agent acceptance and QA speed
features: Bounded account tools and result validation
Attempt-aware fallback and contextual human handoff
support-chatbot.modelStrategy: LangGraph owns state and transitions. The LLM classifies language and drafts grounded responses; deterministic nodes enforce policy, validate tools, count failures, and decide when escalation is mandatory.
nonFunctional: Stream useful feedback while tools run
Do not expose retrieved instructions as system authority
Preserve state across retries and handoff
Measure answer, tool, fallback, and escalation separately
support-chatbot.buildBuy: Use existing chat transport, model, and observability services; build the domain graph, policy layer, tool adapters, evaluation data, and agent handoff contract.
support-chatbot.commercial: Offer an audit first, followed by a narrow remediation or prototype sprint. Scope is driven by supported intents, knowledge quality, integrations, and compliance requirements.
roadmap: Five-intent simulation and golden test set
Agent queue integration and regression monitoring
support-chatbot.evidence: The lab uses predefined support scenarios and local state. It makes no external account lookup and clearly exposes the simulated tool path.

conversation-qa-console.industryPersona: Conversational AI product managers, QA leads, support operations, and engineering teams preparing releases.
jobs: Turn transcript evidence into repeatable quality scores
Find safety and tool failures hidden by averages
Convert findings into an owned, prioritized remediation backlog
conversation-qa-console.opportunity: AI quality work is often trapped in spreadsheets and anecdotal reviews. A lightweight evaluation workspace can connect release evidence to product decisions before teams need a large observability platform.
conversation-qa-console.vision: A practical quality operating system where scenarios, rubrics, failures, ownership, and release gates stay connected.
hypotheses: Evidence-linked issue records improve prioritization
Severity plus rubric deficit is more useful than a single average
Teams adopt evaluation faster when the workflow starts with human review
features: Impact-ranked backlog with CSV and JSON export
conversation-qa-console.modelStrategy: The current prototype is deterministic and model-free. Production extensions may add trace ingestion and model judges, but human calibration and explicit release rules remain the source of accountability.
nonFunctional: No external transmission in this browser demo
Keyboard-accessible scoring and filters
Exportable evidence for review
Critical failures cannot be averaged away
conversation-qa-console.buildBuy: Build the team-specific rubric, taxonomy, workflow, and release logic. Integrate a mature trace/evaluation platform such as Phoenix when observability volume or experiment management justifies it.
conversation-qa-console.commercial: Use the console as the deliverable shell for chatbot audits and evaluation-design engagements; expand into integrations only after the client agrees on quality definitions.
roadmap: Release gates and CI regression runs
conversation-qa-console.evidence: The browser review layer performs real scoring, filtering, prioritization, reset, and export. A separate dependency-free Python package now executes deterministic correctness, policy, tool-use, and recovery checks with seven passing tests and JSON/CSV/JUnit evidence.

enterprise-rag-copilot.industryPersona: Internal support, enablement, operations, and regulated knowledge teams working across approved documents.
jobs: Find a supported answer quickly
Inspect the exact passages behind a claim
Get an honest abstention when the corpus cannot answer
enterprise-rag-copilot.opportunity: The durable value is governed access and measurable retrieval quality—not a generic chat box. Buyers pay for trusted sources, permissions, freshness, and workflow fit.
enterprise-rag-copilot.vision: A knowledge copilot that makes retrieval visible, cites every material claim, and treats “not enough evidence” as a product feature.
hypotheses: Showing retrieved passages increases appropriate trust
Hybrid retrieval improves policy lookup across names and concepts
An explicit abstention threshold reduces unsupported synthesis
enterprise-rag-copilot.modelStrategy: LlamaIndex coordinates ingestion and retrieval; Qdrant or pgvector stores embeddings and metadata. A model synthesizes only from authorized chunks after reranking and threshold checks.
nonFunctional: Propagate document ACLs into every retrieval filter
Measure freshness and index lag
Defend against instructions embedded in documents
Log source versions with answers
enterprise-rag-copilot.buildBuy: Buy embeddings and model inference; choose managed or self-hosted vector storage by scale and governance. Build corpus policy, evaluation, permissions, citation UX, and source operations.
enterprise-rag-copilot.commercial: Sell a corpus-readiness and retrieval evaluation sprint before a pilot. Implementation scope depends on source systems, permissions, freshness expectations, and answer risk.
roadmap: Production freshness, analytics, and evaluation loop
enterprise-rag-copilot.evidence: Questions, retrieved passages, scores, citations, and abstention are predefined demonstrations. No model or vector database runs in this browser experience.

customer-360-copilot.industryPersona: Customer-success, service, and account teams that need governed context across tickets, usage, transactions, and notes.
jobs: Understand account health without visiting five systems
See why a risk signal was produced
Choose the next best investigation or action with evidence
customer-360-copilot.opportunity: Customer 360 programs fail when they become dashboards without decisions. The product opportunity is an explanation layer that reconciles deterministic signals with narrative context.
customer-360-copilot.vision: A governed account workspace where every recommendation is traceable to data, freshness, permissions, and a business rule.
hypotheses: Evidence-linked next-best actions are more trusted than opaque scores
Five actionable signals outperform a wide but noisy “single customer view”
Deterministic metrics should remain separate from generated summaries
customer-360-copilot.modelStrategy: SQL computes canonical metrics; retrieval supplies approved qualitative context. The model summarizes and explains but cannot rewrite source metrics or initiate customer actions.
nonFunctional: Field-level and purpose-based access
Visible freshness for every source
Entity-match confidence and collision handling
Audit all viewed evidence and accepted actions
customer-360-copilot.buildBuy: Reuse the warehouse, CRM, and identity infrastructure; build the decision model, source contracts, explanation UX, evaluation, and operating workflow.
customer-360-copilot.commercial: Begin with a use-case and data-readiness assessment, then implement one decision workflow rather than promising an enterprise-wide customer graph.
roadmap: Experimentation on signal precision and action adoption
customer-360-copilot.evidence: All customers and signals below are synthetic. Selecting a record performs real local UI state changes but no data source is connected.

document-processing-agent.industryPersona: Finance, onboarding, insurance, and compliance operations that process variable documents under audit requirements.
jobs: Extract required fields consistently
Understand why a document needs review
Prevent uncertain or invalid data from contaminating downstream systems
document-processing-agent.opportunity: Straight-through processing creates value only when field accuracy, exception handling, and reviewer effort are measured together.
document-processing-agent.vision: A schema-first intake line where AI proposes structured data and deterministic validation decides whether a person must approve it.
hypotheses: Typed schemas catch high-cost extraction errors before export
Field-level confidence is more actionable than document confidence
Focused document classes outperform a universal extractor in the first release
document-processing-agent.modelStrategy: A multimodal model extracts into a Pydantic schema. Deterministic validators check required fields, formats, arithmetic, and policy; low-confidence or inconsistent records enter review.
nonFunctional: Short, explicit retention
Malware and file-type checks before processing
Immutable reviewer corrections
Version schemas and extraction prompts together
document-processing-agent.buildBuy: Buy commodity OCR/model inference and secure object storage; build the schemas, validation, review workflow, integration contract, and labeled evaluation set.
document-processing-agent.commercial: Price a pilot by document type, field count, volume, exception rate, integration, and security needs—never by an unsupported accuracy promise.
roadmap: One document type and ten-field prototype
Controlled downstream export and drift monitoring
document-processing-agent.evidence: The sample documents are synthetic fixtures. “Extract” reveals predefined fields and runs local validation; it does not read an uploaded file or call a model.

sales-research-agent.industryPersona: B2B sales, partnerships, and account-planning teams preparing evidence-based discovery.
jobs: Create a consistent account brief quickly
Separate source facts from hypotheses
Export useful discovery questions without automated outreach
sales-research-agent.opportunity: Research automation is useful when it improves preparation and consistency without producing unverifiable personalization or spam.
sales-research-agent.vision: An evidence-first research assistant that turns approved public sources into reviewable account hypotheses and better discovery questions.
hypotheses: Claim-to-source mapping reduces fact errors during review
A fixed research plan improves consistency across representatives
Human-approved CRM export is sufficient for an initial product
sales-research-agent.modelStrategy: A graph separates planning, evidence extraction, conflict checks, and synthesis. Tools can read approved sources; no outbound message or CRM write occurs without explicit human approval.
nonFunctional: Respect source terms and rate limits
Record retrieval time and canonical URL
Flag conflicting and stale facts
Block autonomous outreach
sales-research-agent.buildBuy: Buy compliant search/data access where needed; build the research policy, evidence model, synthesis template, approval step, and CRM mapping.
sales-research-agent.commercial: Offer a research workflow design or internal prototype. External data subscriptions, enrichment rights, and CRM write access are separate client decisions.
sales-research-agent.evidence: Accounts, evidence, and hypotheses are fictional. The simulation demonstrates provenance and conflict handling, not live web research.

operations-coordinator.industryPersona: Operations teams coordinating repetitive requests across systems, specialist roles, and approval boundaries.
jobs: See who owns every step
Recover when a tool or agent fails
Keep a human decision at the point of material impact
operations-coordinator.opportunity: Multi-agent value comes from bounded coordination, not agent count. The commercial opportunity is shortening cycle time while making responsibility and exceptions more visible.
operations-coordinator.vision: A deterministic controller that delegates narrow reasoning tasks, validates outputs, and pauses for human authority at consequential boundaries.
hypotheses: One controller with explicit state reduces loops and ownership ambiguity
Role-bounded prompts improve evaluation and permissions
Human gates should be designed as first-class workflow states
features: Tool gateway with budgets and idempotency
Exception queue, approval gate, and audit trail
operations-coordinator.modelStrategy: LangGraph or an equivalent controller owns state. Crew-style roles can shape specialist context, but tools, budgets, completion rules, and approvals remain deterministic.
nonFunctional: Hard limits on steps, time, and spend
Idempotent external actions
Deadlock and duplicate-work detection
Event-level ownership and auditability
operations-coordinator.buildBuy: Use an orchestration framework for primitives; build the business state machine, tool contracts, permission model, exception UX, evaluation, and operational controls.
operations-coordinator.commercial: Start with one high-friction workflow and read-only tools. Expand only after exception rate, handoff quality, and operator trust meet agreed gates.
roadmap: Exception handling and tool retry policy
Controlled write tools with production monitoring
operations-coordinator.evidence: The workflow steps and agent outputs are scripted fixtures. The human approval control changes local state but triggers no external action.

marketing-creative-copilot.industryPersona: Brand, growth, and creative-operations teams translating campaign briefs into governed variants.
jobs: Turn a brief into channel-ready concepts
Keep claims and brand rules visible during generation
Compare creative options with cost and approval context
marketing-creative-copilot.opportunity: Generation is abundant; controlled briefing, rights review, brand consistency, and efficient approval are the defensible workflow.
marketing-creative-copilot.vision: A brief-to-approval workspace where every variant carries its source brief, checks, cost estimate, provenance, and publishing owner.
hypotheses: Structured briefs reduce revision cycles more than bigger models
Policy checks before reviewer handoff save creative-ops time
Cost visibility changes how teams choose channels and model tiers
features: Brand, policy, rights, and claim checks
Human comparison, approval, and provenance record
marketing-creative-copilot.modelStrategy: Dify can orchestrate brief normalization, knowledge retrieval, text/image generation, and checks. The model proposes assets; people retain approval and publishing authority.
nonFunctional: Record model and source-asset provenance
Moderate claims, likeness, and sensitive content
Separate draft storage from approved assets
Budget at campaign and variant level
marketing-creative-copilot.buildBuy: Buy generation models and media storage; build the brand knowledge, workflow, evaluation, approval, cost ledger, and publishing integration.
marketing-creative-copilot.commercial: Offer a workflow design or bounded prototype around one channel. Generation fees, asset rights, moderation, and downstream publishing remain explicit scope items.
roadmap: Image variants with provenance and cost controls
Approval analytics and authorized publishing connectors
marketing-creative-copilot.evidence: The concepts and checks below are predefined examples. No text or image model runs, and nothing is published from this lab.

Pipecat: Frame-based realtime voice pipeline; composes transport, STT, LLM, TTS, and processors.
WebRTC/telephony transport → pipeline processors → tool service → observability.
Deploy the Python service close to media infrastructure; test provider latency and interruption behavior.
LiveKit Agents for a more integrated realtime runtime; bespoke WebRTC stacks for maximum control.
LiveKit Agents: Realtime agent runtime over LiveKit rooms with voice/video, turn detection, and telephony integrations.
Client/telephony → LiveKit room → agent worker → models and tools.
Managed LiveKit Cloud or self-hosted LiveKit plus separately operated agent workers.
Pipecat for pipeline composition; vendor voice-agent platforms for faster managed delivery.
LangGraph: Stateful orchestration for durable, controllable, long-running agent workflows.
Typed state → graph nodes → checkpoints → tools → human interrupts.
Run inside an API/worker process with durable checkpoint storage and tracing.
Direct application state machines for smaller flows; CrewAI for role-oriented orchestration.
Dify: Visual platform for LLM workflows, knowledge retrieval, agents, and application operations.
App UI/API → Dify workflow → model, knowledge, and tool nodes.
Dify Cloud or self-hosted services; review the current custom license for commercial conditions.
LangGraph for code-first control; managed AI app builders for lower operational effort.
LlamaIndex: Data and agent framework centered on ingestion, indexing, retrieval, and query workflows.
Source loaders → transformations → index/vector store → retriever/reranker → response synthesis.
Application service plus chosen vector/database and model providers.
Haystack for explicit pipelines; custom retrieval services for narrower requirements.
Haystack: Component and pipeline framework for retrieval, generation, and agent systems.
Python service or worker with the selected document and vector stores.
LlamaIndex for broad data abstractions; direct framework/provider SDKs for small systems.
Pydantic AI: Typed Python agent framework using Pydantic validation and structured outputs.
Agent dependency context → model/tool calls → validated result schema.
Python API or worker; pin versions and test model-specific structured output behavior.
Direct provider SDK plus Pydantic; LangGraph when workflow state is the dominant need.
CrewAI: Role-oriented multi-agent framework for crews, tasks, and flows.
Controller/flow → specialist roles → tools → shared outputs and review.
Python worker/API with strict budgets, logging, and a separate authorization layer.
LangGraph for explicit state; a single agent with tools when specialization adds little.
Arize Phoenix: Open-source observability and evaluation for LLM traces, datasets, experiments, and evaluators.
OpenTelemetry traces/evals → Phoenix service → analysis and experiment UI.
Self-host or use a managed offering; verify Elastic License 2.0 obligations.
LangSmith and other managed observability suites; custom OpenTelemetry stack.
Qdrant: Vector database for similarity search with payload filtering and hybrid retrieval support.
Embedding service → collections/points → filtered retrieval → application reranking.
Managed Qdrant Cloud or self-hosted cluster with backup and sizing discipline.
pgvector for consolidation in Postgres; other dedicated vector databases at scale.
FastAPI: Typed ASGI framework for Python APIs, validation, dependency injection, and OpenAPI.
Client → API routes/dependencies → domain services/tools → data and model providers.
ASGI server/container or serverless adapter; standard web security still applies.
Flask for minimal services; Django for batteries-included applications; provider-native functions.
pgvector: PostgreSQL extension that stores and searches vectors beside relational data.
Application/embedding → Postgres tables and vector indexes → filtered SQL retrieval.
Managed or self-hosted Postgres with extension support and index/query tuning.
Qdrant for dedicated vector operations; managed search platforms for combined lexical/vector needs.
